title: Why Franklin fed his crew seal blubber
topic: Why the British explorer Sir John Franklin ordered his crew to eat seal blubber (Arctic, 1845)

lines: Sir John Franklin forces his men to chew raw seal blubber on ice.
The crew grumbles, calling the order madness.
Some swear they’ll starve before they swallow any more animal fat.
Ice traps the ships for months.
Rations run low, and every day the men grow weaker.
You see, it’s like skipping breakfast and the only snack left is a greasy doughnut.
Seal blubber is dense with calories and fat, the same fuel seals use to survive long fasts.
Those calories replace missing meat, and the thick fat slows body‑heat loss in sub‑zero air.
Ironically, the blubber could not replace the lost vitamin C and thiamine, so scurvy and beri‑beri still claimed the crew.

claims.claim: Seal blubber provides dense calories and fat that serve as energy and insulation for fasting animals.
The Franklin expedition suffered severe vitamin‑C and thiamine deficiencies that contributed to its death.
